subject: Peak vs Sustained QPS — Narrowing profile & next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@ordermart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-12T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Peak vs Sustained QPS — Narrowing profile & next steps

Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick post-call recap and a focused ask to help us finalize a throughput recommendation and a canary plan. Attaching the workload snapshot you shared in the call.

Recap (from what we saw):
- Primary workload: Order confirmation + cart suggestions (multi-turn chat + streaming partials).
- Avg tokens per request (stated): ~510 tokens.
- Observed steady-state QPS: roughly 30–40 QPS.
- Observed short peaks during promotional windows: spikes up to ~160–200 QPS lasting 2–6 minutes.
- Streaming: ~65% of requests use streaming; typical stream duration 1.5–4s.

What we need to finalize sizing: three discrete clarifications so we can (1) map to tokens/sec and concurrency for infra, and (2) propose SLOs/canary thresholds.
1) Confirm average tokens per request across endpoints (cart-suggest vs order-confirm) — you mentioned 510, but can you confirm split?
2) Confirm peak cadence: are peaks sustained (e.g., 30 minutes) or short bursts (2–6 minutes)? You said promotional moments are short but want exact durations for our cost modeling.
3) Streaming concurrency: of the peak QPS, what % are streaming sessions vs plain responses? We captured ~65% in call notes but please confirm.

Requested artifacts (attached): workload-snapshot-ordermart-20270812.csv (we added a column for stream_flag), and a draft SLO mapping PDF. Please reply with the three clarifications.

Next steps (proposed):
- You confirm numbers above by EOD Aug 14.
- We produce a tailored throughput-sizing sheet and an initial canary playbook by Aug 19.
- Joint review (30m) week of Aug 23 to lock capacity and SLA.

Thanks — kim

--
Kimberly Park
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: workload-snapshot-ordermart-20270812.csv (CSV, 42 KB); slo-mapping-draft-ORD-4731.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@ordermart.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: OrderMart SRE <sre@ordermart.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-13T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Peak vs Sustained QPS — Narrowing profile & next steps

Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap. Answers inline below.

1) Avg tokens per request: overall average 510 is correct. Breakdown:
   - order-confirm (single-turn): ~220 tokens avg
   - cart-suggest (multi-turn / streaming): ~740 tokens avg (this is why overall avg is 510)

2) Peak cadence: two patterns:
   - Short promotional bursts: 2–8 minutes, QPS up to ~180–210 (we saw a 6-minute 200 QPS burst during last sale).
   - Sustained daily evening surge: ~30–45 minutes, QPS bump to 90–110.

3) Streaming % at peak: during promo bursts streaming remains at ~60–70% of requests. During sustained evening surge streaming drops to ~50%.

Extra context: our tolerance for tail latency is tight for cart-suggest (affects UX). We aim for p95 < 150ms and p99 < 400ms for serving the first token; end-to-end interaction can be longer because client assembles stream.

I'll attach a small CSV slice we exported after the call (same filename you attached). Happy to hop on the 30m review — Aug 24/25 morning PT works for my team.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product Engineering, OrderMart
alex.johnson@ordermart.com

Attachment referenced: workload-snapshot-ordermart-20270812.csv (filtered sample)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@ordermart.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-17T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Peak vs Sustained QPS — Narrowing profile & next steps

Alex — great detail, thank you. A couple of targeted asks so we can convert your numbers into tokens/sec & concurrency for the sizing sheet:

- For the promo bursts: can you give 3 representative burst samples (start/end timestamps + peak QPS) from the last month? Even rough timestamps are fine — we only need duration distribution.
- For streaming sessions: can you provide the distribution of stream durations (percentiles: p50, p75, p90)? That helps us model steady-state concurrency vs transient open streams.
- For request mix during peaks: approximate % split between order-confirm vs cart-suggest (we're assuming 25% / 75% during promos, confirm or correct).

Our internal modeling notes (for transparency):
- We convert QPS -> tokens/sec using your per-request token averages.
- Steady-state target size: provision for 1.5x steady-state tokens/sec, autoscale to absorb 2x short bursts with warm caches.
- Canary thresholds we propose:
  * p95 token-latency < 150ms for first token
  * error rate < 0.5% during canary window
  * no more than 10% request degradation compared to baseline model

If you can drop the three small artifacts by EOD Aug 18 we can ship the initial sizing and canary playbook on Aug 19 as planned.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Solution Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@ordermart.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Peak vs Sustained QPS — Narrowing profile & next steps

Alex — thanks for the follow-ups and Marissa for the modeling notes. Action summary and what Redwood will deliver next (concrete):

Action items for OrderMart (please confirm):
- Provide three promo-burst samples (start/end timestamps + peak QPS) — due: 2027-08-18 (if possible).
- Provide stream duration percentiles (p50/p75/p90) — due: 2027-08-18.
- Confirm peak request mix order-confirm vs cart-suggest — due: 2027-08-18.

What Redwood will deliver by 2027-08-19:
- Throughput sizing sheet (CSV): tokens/sec, concurrent streams, buffer sizing, and cost estimate at steady vs peak. (attached: workload-snapshot-ordermart-20270812.csv updated).
- Canary playbook (doc): traffic split for canary, fallback model mapping, metric thresholds (p95/p99 targets & error thresholds). (attached: slo-mapping-draft-ORD-4731.pdf).
- Suggested runtime knobs: batching target (per-GPU qps), prefix/KV cache warm-up recommendations, and streaming concurrency limits.

Proposed review: Aug 24, 10:00–10:30 PT — Kimberly to send invite; Alex please confirm.

If OrderMart can confirm the items above, we'll size for:
- Steady-state provisioning: ~45k tokens/sec (1.5x steady), which maps to ~88 concurrent streaming sessions assuming avg tokens and a 3s token emission window.
- Peak-handling target (short bursts): autoscale headroom to absorb 2x peak (~200k tokens/sec) for up to 8 minutes with graceful fallback to smaller quantized model if required.

Thanks all — Ben

--
